summary: Recent election results are generating renewed momentum for D.C. statehood advocacy, with advocates noting that midterm outcomes have revived the push for full representation. Separately, statehood supporters have highlighted D.C.'s population size compared to existing states and documented what they describe as recent attacks on the District's local authority. Without statehood, D.C. residents have no senators, and their one delegate to the House cannot vote on the House floor.
